full_judgment: 3. Facts, relevant for disposal of both these the Rules, in brief, are that, the present petitioner Azizur Rahman filed Miscellaneous (pre-emption) Case No. 12 of 1999, under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, before the court of Assistant Judge, Jointapur, Sylhet, against Cherag Ali and 3 others (the purchasers/pre-emptee) and Haji Habibur Rahman is the seller-opposite party, while there are 9 others as the pro-forma opposite parties. The main contention of the petitioner is that 39 decimals of cultivable land, comprising the entire property of SA plot No. 169 of SA khatian No. 169, Mouza Thakurermati, PS Jointapur, District-Sylhet, fell into the shares of Shorbanu Bibi (the pro-forma opposite party No. 12), pursuant to the partition between her and other co-sharers. That Sarban Bibi, by a registered deed No. 8845 dated 21-8-1963, sold her entire 39 decimals of the suit property to Haji Habibur Rahman (seller)-opposite party No. 5. Thereafter, the said Haji Habibur Rahman has sold his entire 39 decimals of land lying at SA plot No. 169 to Cherag Ali and 3 others, vide sale deed No. 494 dated 3-3-1999 (Exhibit 2). Further contention of the petitioner is that, on 14-3-1999, he got to know, from some farmers, that the suit property has been purchased by the opposite party Nos. 1-4, from opposite party No. 5. Further case of the petitioner is that, he is the co-sharer in the SA khatian No. 169 of Mouza Thakurermati (Exhibit 1), but he was not informed by opposite party No. 1 about the intention to sell the suit property and no notice was given to him, under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Therefore, he came to know about the sale of the property before 14-3-1999 and that he is a co-sharer of the suit property and the suit property is adjacent to his property and the suit property is needed to him.
